g1|variants|rush order.summary: Rush orders in SAP S/4HANA OTC trigger immediate delivery creation upon sales order saving, allowing same-day fulfillment. Variants differ by whether billing is created immediately alongside the delivery or generated separately through regular billing runs.

variants.name: Standard Rush Order with Immediate Delivery and Immediate Billing
variants.when_used: Used when the customer places a rush order requiring same-day delivery and the corresponding billing document must be generated immediately upon goods issue.
variants.key_config: Sales document type RO configured with immediate delivery creation active, and billing type F2 tied to immediate billing generation via copy control from delivery to billing.

variants.name: Rush Order with Immediate Delivery and Periodic Billing
variants.when_used: Used when the customer requires immediate delivery for urgent needs, but billing is consolidated and processed periodically through background billing runs.
variants.key_config: Sales document type RO configured for immediate delivery creation, but billing type is set to invoice request F1 for periodic billing due lists (VF04).

g1|core|rush order|standard rush order w.title: Rush Order with Immediate Delivery and Immediate Billing
g1|core|rush order|standard rush order w.story: Imagine a superhero who gets an urgent call and instantly delivers the package while handing over the receipt at the exact same second. In SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash, a rush order creates a sales document that automatically triggers an outbound delivery and an immediate billing document in one streamlined run. When this fails, customers wait too long for their goods and invoices get stuck in processing queues. Rush orders keep cash velocity high and bypass standard multi-step fulfillment delays.
g1|core|rush order|standard rush order w.why_business_needs_it: This process satisfies high-priority customer demands by collapsing order entry, picking, delivery creation, and billing into a single continuous transaction. It minimizes lead time for urgent product requests and accelerates revenue recognition.

modules.hands_off_to: LE (Logistics Execution) to automatically generate the outbound delivery document and goods movement.
FI (Financial Accounting) and SD Billing for invoice creation.

prerequisites: Material Master Data with Sales and Plant views (MM01)
Pricing Conditions and Procedure setup (VK11 / V/08)

config_steps.step: Define Sales Document Types for standard rush orders
config_steps.where: VOV8 -- SPRO > Sales and Distribution > Sales > Sales Documents > Sales Document Header > Define Sales Document Types
config_steps.values: Sales Doc Type: ZRO1; Immediate delivery: X; Dlv Type: LF; Billing type: F2
config_steps.check: Run SE16N on table TVAK for document type ZRO1 and verify that field AUTLF (Immediate Delivery) is set to X.
config_steps.why: Rush orders need to skip manual fulfillment steps, so this setting forces SAP to create the delivery document automatically the second the sales order is saved.
config_steps.if_missing: Without this flag, rush orders behave like standard orders and sit unfulfilled in the sales queue, failing the immediate delivery service level agreement (message V1556).
actions: Enter /nVOV8 in the command field and press Enter
Select standard sales document type RO and click Copy As (F6)
Overwrite Sales Doc. Type with ZRO1 and Description with "Standard Rush Order"
In the General Control section, set Checking group to 02 and check the Immediate delivery indicator X
In the Billing Document section, set Dlv. related bl.ing to blank and Billing type to F2
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign to customizing transport request

fields.note: Blank to allow immediate billing upon delivery creation

config_steps.why: SAP needs to know which shipping point and delivery type to invoke for a specific sales area when an immediate delivery flag is active.
config_steps.if_missing: If this assignment is missing, the immediate delivery fails upon saving the order with a missing shipping point error (message VL382).
actions: Enter /nOVLK in the command field and press Enter
Click New Entries
Enter Sales Organization 1000, Distr. Channel 10, Division 00, Order Type ZRO1
Enter Shipping Point 1000 and Delivery Type LF
Save (Ctrl+S) and assign to transport request

g1|core|rush order|rush order with immed.title: Rush Order with Immediate Delivery and Periodic Billing
g1|core|rush order|rush order with immed.story: A customer needs goods today and cannot wait for the regular delivery run, so the sales team enters a high-priority order that immediately triggers a warehouse shipment while collecting the invoice amounts into a batch billing run at the end of the month. Formally, this is an Order-to-Cash process utilizing sales document type RO which simultaneously creates outbound delivery LF upon saving, utilizing schedule line category CP, and later aggregates billing documents of type F1 via periodic batch processing.
g1|core|rush order|rush order with immed.why_business_needs_it: It captures urgent customer demand immediately by forcing the creation of an outbound delivery at sales order save, minimizing fulfillment lead times while keeping administrative costs low through consolidated periodic billing. This balances rapid physical service with efficient financial processing.

modules.hands_off_to: LE (Logistics Execution) to pick, pack, and post goods issue.

modules.role: Processes outbound delivery LF and posts goods issue based on immediate triggers from the rush order.
modules.hands_off_to: FI (Financial Accounting) for general ledger updates upon goods issue and billing.

modules.role: Receives accounting postings from goods issue and periodic billing type F1.

errors.prevent: Always ensure that every new sales document type intended for immediate delivery has the automatic delivery indicator active and complete shipping point determination paths assigned before transport.

best_practices.practice: Configure sales document type RO in transaction VOV8 with immediate delivery creation indicator set to 'X'.
best_practices.why: This ensures the system automatically triggers outbound delivery generation immediately upon saving the rush order without manual intervention.

best_practices.practice: Schedule background job SD_VBRK_RESOURCE via transaction SM36 for periodic billing run execution.
best_practices.why: Automating periodic billing batches for rush order variants prevents invoice backlogs and smooths out system processing loads.

best_practices.practice: Monitor unbilled deliveries daily using transaction VL04 or SAP Fiori app 'Process Outbound Deliveries'.
best_practices.why: Proactive monitoring catches stuck deliveries where goods issue occurred but immediate billing failed to trigger.

best_practices.practice: Maintain specific pricing procedures in transaction V/08 for rush orders to bypass standard quotation validity checks.
best_practices.why: Rush orders require immediate price validity without relying on long-term agreement checks that can slow down document processing.

best_practices.practice: Assign dedicated shipping points in transaction OVXC for rush order plant determinations.
best_practices.why: Isolating rush order fulfillment paths prevents urgent orders from getting queued behind bulk warehouse picking tasks.

best_practices.practice: Validate availability check control in transaction OVZ9 with scope of check excluding future receipts for rush orders.
best_practices.why: Rush orders demand physical stock on hand; including future replenishment leads to immediate delivery fulfillment failures.

best_practices.practice: Implement output determination condition records in transaction VV31 for output type RD00 with dispatch time 4.
best_practices.why: Dispatch time 4 ensures immediate printing or electronic transmission of the invoice as soon as the billing document is saved.

best_practices.practice: Review credit management risk categories in transaction OVA8 specifically for rush order document categories.
best_practices.why: Fine-tuning credit checks prevents false-positive credit blocks from delaying legitimate same-day shipments to trusted customers.

g1|panel|rush order.otc_impact: The rush order scenario family sits at the intersection of urgent sales execution and accelerated financial settlement within Order-to-Cash. It radically compresses the order-to-delivery-to-billing timeline by automatically generating an immediate outbound delivery upon sales order save and triggering parallel or subsequent billing. This impacts customer satisfaction by enabling same-day fulfillment while tightly binding logistics execution to credit and inventory availability checks.

panel_qa.question: How do we balance immediate delivery creation in rush orders with rigorous credit management checks without delaying the customer?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Rush orders require synchronous credit checks at sales order creation to prevent bad debt before physical goods leave the warehouse. We configure Automatic Credit Management using SAP Credit Management (FI-CR) with credit check rules assigned to the rush order sales document type. If the credit check fails, the order receives a delivery block, halting the immediate delivery creation process until released via transaction VKM1. This protects the company's bottom line while maintaining automated compliance. Next, we will review the credit check configuration steps to ensure zero latency.
panel_qa.trap: We just turn off credit checks for rush orders so they go out the door instantly.

panel_qa.question: What architectural safeguards prevent inventory discrepancies when rush orders trigger immediate deliveries against stock that might be reserved for planned orders?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Rush orders bypass standard picking queues by triggering delivery creation immediately upon order save, making real-time availability check (ATP) critical. We configure the Availability Check (ATP) in SD requirement classes using checking rule B and scope of check including safety stock and current stock. If stock is unavailable, backorder processing or substitution rules must trigger immediately within the sales order. This prevents overselling and ensures physical stock aligns with financial postings. Next, we validate the schedule line category configuration to ensure proper requirements type assignment.
panel_qa.trap: We rely on the warehouse workers to fix stock shortages manually when they pick the rush order.

panel_qa.question: What is the cash flow and Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) impact of choosing immediate billing versus periodic billing for rush orders?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Choosing immediate billing for rush orders accelerates revenue recognition and invoice dispatch to the same day as shipment, directly improving DSO. We implement billing type RO (Rush Invoice) tied to immediate delivery-related billing processing in transaction VTFL. Periodic billing, conversely, aggregates rush shipments into weekly or monthly consolidated invoices, increasing working capital requirements but reducing customer invoice processing fatigue. We align the billing variant with the customer master billing profile in XD03. Next, we will monitor billing block release metrics in standard Fiori analytics.
panel_qa.trap: We bill everything periodically because it saves paper, regardless of cash flow goals.

panel_qa.question: How do we handle delivery blocks when a rush order is entered by customer service for a key account with disputed invoices?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: When a key account has disputed invoices, the credit management system places a credit hold on the rush order. We configure reason for credit check blocks to automatically set the delivery block field VBUV-LIFSP in the sales order table VBAK. This stops the immediate delivery creation job from picking up the order until the credit department resolves the dispute. This strict gatekeeping prevents financial leakage while providing an audit trail. Next, we will audit the user roles authorized for mass release of delivery blocks.
panel_qa.trap: Customer service agents have override keys to remove delivery blocks whenever a customer complains.

panel_qa.question: What is the exact master data and pricing setup required to ensure rush orders do not mistakenly apply standard contract or volume rebates?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Rush orders often carry premium pricing or expedited freight surcharges that differ from standard contract terms. We configure a dedicated sales document type RO with specific pricing procedure assignment in transaction V/08. This procedure includes condition types for emergency handling fees and excludes standard rebate condition types where company policy dictates. The pricing type in the copy control from sales order to billing ensures manual price overrides are preserved or recalculated per business rules. Next, we will test the pricing determination log for edge cases.
panel_qa.trap: We use the standard pricing procedure and manually type in the rush surcharge on every line item.

panel_qa.question: How do we monitor and resolve stuck immediate deliveries where warehouse task creation fails after the rush order is saved?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: When an immediate delivery fails to generate a warehouse task in Extended Warehouse Management (EWM), orders stall between OTC and logistics execution. We utilize SAP Fiori app 'Monitor Outbound Deliveries' (app ID VL06O) and EWM queue monitor /SCWM/QWO to identify intermediate message communication errors. We configure ALE/IDoc or qRFC error handling with automatic notification to the warehouse supervisor. This proactive monitoring ensures the rush promise is kept or exception handling is triggered immediately. Next, we will implement automated alert thresholds for unpicked rush deliveries.
panel_qa.trap: We wait for the customer to call asking where their rush order is before we look for stuck deliveries.

doc_flow.what: Sales order of type RO is created, initiating immediate outbound delivery creation upon save.
Delivery document of type LF is automatically generated from the rush order for warehouse processing.
Inventory is issued via movement type 601, updating delivery status to completely issued.
Periodic billing runs generate invoice type F1, consolidating delivered orders for accounting transfer.

test_cases.title: Happy Path - Rush Order with Immediate Delivery and Periodic Billing
test_cases.preconditions: Customer master, material master with stock, and condition records exist in sales area 1000/10/00.

steps.step: Create sales order of type RO
steps.data: Order Type: RO, Sales Org: 1000, Dist Channel: 10, Division: 00, Sold-to: 100000, Material: TG11, Qty: 10
steps.expected: Sales order saved and immediate outbound delivery triggered automatically.

steps.data: Delivery Type: LF, Delivery Number from previous step
steps.expected: Delivery is displayed with schedule line category CP and picking/packing status open.
Goods issue posted with movement type 601, material document generated.

steps.data: Sales Organization: 1000, Billing Date: Current Date
steps.expected: Billing document of type F1 is created successfully.

test_cases.expected_result: Rush order RO successfully processed through delivery LF, goods issue, and periodic billing F1.
test_cases.documents_created: Rush Order RO 1000001, Delivery LF 8000001, Material Document 49000001, Billing F1 9000001

test_cases.title: Negative Test - Missing Inventory for Rush Order Delivery
test_cases.preconditions: Material master exists but has zero stock in storage location.

steps.step: Attempt to create rush order with zero stock material
steps.data: Order Type: RO, Sold-to: 100000, Material: ZERO_STOCK, Qty: 100
steps.expected: System attempts to create delivery upon save but fails due to stock insufficiency.

test_cases.expected_result: Delivery creation fails with delivery log error message.
test_cases.documents_created: Rush Order RO 1000002 created, but delivery creation fails with message VL369 (No stock available).

test_cases.title: Edge Case - Billing Block on Periodic Billing Run
test_cases.preconditions: Rush order created with a manual billing block assigned at header level.

steps.step: Create rush order with billing block
steps.data: Order Type: RO, Sold-to: 100000, Material: TG11, Qty: 5, Billing Block: 01
steps.expected: Order saved, delivery created, goods issue posted.

steps.data: Sales Org: 1000, Billing Date: Current Date
steps.expected: Order is bypassed in billing due to active billing block.

test_cases.expected_result: Billing document is not generated for the blocked order until the block is removed.
test_cases.documents_created: Rush Order RO 1000003, Delivery LF 8000003, Material Document 49000003, No billing document created.
